findings.issue_text: [BUG] EventManager's create path dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration with no null guard, so it throws a TypeError whenever evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array and the event location is Google Meet. Booking creation and confirmation 500 with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)' for users with no destinationCalendar — handleNewBooking sets destinationCalendar to null when neither eventType nor organizer has one, and confirm.handler passes [] — which is precisely the Meet-selected-without-Google-Calendar case this fallback line exists to handle; the old optional-chained comparison fell back to Cal Video instead of crashing.

[BUG] The slug spread condition was inverted from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug } to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}, so the Organization create no longer receives a slug when team billing is disabled. On every deployment with IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED false (the default for self-hosted installs), Prisma rejects the create because the required slug argument is missing and organization creation returns a 500; with the flag true the slug is additionally assigned immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug approval gating that the adjacent metadata line implements.

[BUG] updateEvent's fallback predicate event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it compares every calendar's externalId against null/undefined and can never match, leaving selectedCalendar undefined where the old code returned destinationCalendar.externalId. Rescheduling a booking whose calendar reference carries no externalCalendarId — which includes every booking created through EventManager's no-credentialId path, since that path now stores result.externalId (undefined) on the reference — calls calendar.events.update with calendarId undefined, googleapis throws Missing required parameter, and the Google event is never updated.

[BUG] deleteEvent's fallback event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId is evaluated only in the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so the predicate can never match a real calendar and calendarId is always undefined in that branch. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId invokes calendar.events.delete with calendarId undefined, which googleapis rejects, so the Google event is orphaned on the host's calendar after the Cal.com booking is gone.

[BUG] The new per-reference loop reuses the single function-scoped credential variable, so a reference whose credentialId resolves to neither a calendarCredential nor a DB row runs updateEvent with the previous reference's credential, or with undefined on the first iteration. A multi-calendar booking whose later reference points at a deleted or inaccessible credential gets that reference's uid and externalCalendarId pushed to the previous credential's calendar service — a wrong-calendar update that 404s and leaves the event stale — while an unresolvable first reference makes getCalendar(undefined) throw and rejects the entire reschedule.

[BUG] The DB fallback assigns the raw prisma.credential.findUnique result — fetched without the app relation, hence with no appName — into calendarCredential and hands it to getCalendar, which resolves the integration from credential.appName. getCalendar returns null for the appName-less credential, so calendar?.deleteEvent(...) is a silent no-op: cancelling the collective bookings this PR targets, whose reference credentialId belongs to a teammate or team rather than bookingToDelete.user, leaves the event live on that calendar with no error surfaced.

[BUG] createEvent now selects the target calendar solely via destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId), so a destination calendar without a credentialId — the case EventManager's else-branch exists to serve — never matches and the event is written to 'primary' instead of the destination's configured externalId. Bookings against a credentialId-less destination calendar now land in each connected Google credential's primary calendar (duplicating the event once per credential) instead of the user's selected calendar, and the stored reference ends up with a wrong or missing externalCalendarId that later reschedule/cancel paths depend on.

[BUG] Office365CalendarService.createEvent builds eventsUrl from the first destination calendar's externalId no matter which host's credential is invoking it, so the per-destination creation loop this PR adds still targets the first host's calendar for every host. For a collective booking with multiple Office365 hosts, the secondary host's creation posts to /me/calendars/{first host's calendar id}/events under the second host's token, Microsoft Graph returns 404, and the secondary host's calendar never receives the event — the multi-host fix only works for Google.

[BUG] LarkCalendarService.createEvent resolves calendarId from the first destination calendar only, ignoring which destination and credential the EventManager loop is currently processing. For collective bookings with multiple Lark hosts, the secondary host's createEvent calls the Lark API with the first host's calendar ID under the wrong credential, the call errors, and that host's calendar never gets the event — the PR's multi-host handling is unimplemented for Lark.

[ADVISORY] The recurring-series deletion sweep over all user calendar credentials and all updatedBookings now runs once per calendar reference, and inside the sweep each updated booking is still handled via references.find, i.e. only its first calendar reference. Cancelling a multi-reference recurring collective booking issues references x credentials duplicate delete calls — every attempt after the first fails and is logged — while the remaining bookings' secondary calendar references are never deleted, orphaning events on teammates' calendars.

[ADVISORY] The reschedule-merge path still deletes only booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes('_calendar')) — a single reference — even though this same diff makes bookings carry multiple calendar references. Rescheduling a collective booking that has calendar references on several hosts deletes only the first host's old event and leaves orphaned events on every other host's calendar.

[ADVISORY] evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and the subsequent evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) then silently skips, dropping every teammate's calendar. A collective booking whose organizer has no destinationCalendar proceeds without any of the teammates' destination calendars and without any error, so no teammate calendar receives the event — the multi-host behavior this PR introduces no-ops for exactly that configuration.

[ADVISORY] loadUsers' new catch maps Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError to HttpError 400, rethrowing server-side database failures as client errors with the raw Prisma message. A Prisma known-request error during user loading (e.g. a P2024 connection-pool timeout) reaches booking clients as 400 Bad Request carrying the raw database error text, so clients treat a transient server fault as a permanent request error and internal DB details leak into the response.

[ADVISORY] createEvent takes the organizer email from the first destination calendar while selecting the target calendar by credentialId, so the event written to a secondary host's calendar carries the first host's externalId as its organizer email. Every multi-host collective booking produces events on secondary hosts' calendars whose organizer is misattributed to the first host's calendar ID, misowning the very events this PR adds.

[BUG] The rewritten slug spread inverts the original gating: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, so the organization slug is now written exactly in the configuration where it was previously withheld. On installs with team billing disabled, organization create persists no slug at all (org slug lookups/URLs fail, or Prisma rejects the create if slug is required); on billing-enabled installs the slug is now set at creation time, defeating the requestedSlug/isOrganizationVerified=false verification flow that the very next line still implements.

[BUG] updateEvent's fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the predicate compares externalId against a falsy value, never matches, and selectedCalendar is always undefined where the old code returned event.destinationCalendar.externalId. Rescheduling any booking whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy bookings, plus new bookings created via the credentialId-less destination branch which this diff now stores as undefined) calls calendar.events.update with calendarId undefined — the Google call fails and the event silently stays at the old time with only a log line.

[BUG] deleteEvent's fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find never matches and calendarId resolves to undefined where the old code fell back to event.destinationCalendar.externalId. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId calls calendar.events.delete with calendarId undefined — the Google event is never removed and remains as an orphan on the host's calendar after the booking is cancelled in Cal.com.

[BUG] Office365CalendarService.createEvent builds the events URL from destinationCalendar[0].externalId regardless of which host's credential is creating the event, ignoring the per-credential destination selection that the array migration requires. For a COLLECTIVE booking with multiple hosts, every non-first host's event is POSTed to /me/calendars/{first host's externalId}/events using the non-first host's token — Graph returns 404, createEvent fails, and that host's calendar never receives the booking while the booking itself succeeds, i.e. the PR's titular feature is dropped for Office 365.

[BUG] LarkCalendarService.createEvent (and createAttendees at ~line 164) resolve calendarId from destinationCalendar[0] only, so the event for any non-first host is created against the first host's calendar id using the wrong host's credential. For multi-host COLLECTIVE bookings on Lark, the non-first hosts' createEvent calls target a calendar id that does not exist under their credential — the Lark API errors and those hosts never get the event, silently, since CalendarManager only logs the failure.

[BUG] The booking row persists only evt.destinationCalendar[0] via `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`, so the multi-host destination set survives nowhere in the DB and every flow that rebuilds a CalendarEvent from booking.destinationCalendar collapses a COLLECTIVE booking back to host 1. Deferred-creation flows rebuild their evt from booking.destinationCalendar — confirm.handler (collective bookings with requiresConfirmation) and the Stripe/PayPal handlePaymentSuccess webhooks (paid collective bookings) then call EventManager.create with only the first host's destination, so those collective bookings get a calendar event on host 1's calendar only and never on the other hosts' calendars.

[BUG] evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null (not []) when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar, making the subsequent `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` a no-op that silently discards every teammate's collected destination calendar. A COLLECTIVE booking whose organizer has no destination calendar drops all teammates' destinationCalendars — their configured destination calendars are ignored and their events land on default calendars via the create-on-all-credentials branch instead of the calendars they configured.

[BUG] BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters the credential's calendars down to those matching destinationCalendar[0].externalId, so when EventManager creates the event on a non-first host's CalDAV credential the filter matches nothing. For multi-host COLLECTIVE bookings on CalDAV, the filter yields an empty calendar list for every non-first host, Promise.all resolves with zero responses and no event is created on that host's calendar — the fan-out requirement is silently dropped for CalDAV.

[BUG] The credentialId-less destination branch calls createEvent(c, event) without destination.externalId (line ~377) while the reference writer now stores `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`, which is undefined on that branch — the old code stored evt.destinationCalendar.externalId. Bookings created through the credentialId-less destination branch get calendar references with externalCalendarId undefined, so their later update/delete falls into the GoogleCalendarService fallback that this same diff broke (undefined calendarId) — those Google events can never be moved or cancelled.

[BUG] The recurring-event delete sweep (`bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith("_calendar")).map(...)` over updatedBookings) now sits inside the per-reference loop without being made reference-aware, so it executes once per calendar reference and still deletes only the first calendar reference of each remaining series booking. Cancelling a recurring COLLECTIVE booking with N calendar references runs the sweep N times (duplicate deleteEvent calls whose failures are swallowed by the surrounding catch) and never touches the non-first hosts' events for the remaining series bookings — those hosts' calendars keep orphaned events.

[ADVISORY] The diff's only test change updates a serialized fixture value (destinationCalendar: []) and adds no verification of the new multi-destination behavior — the EventManager fan-out loop, Google's per-credential calendar selection, the DB credential fallback, multi-reference update/delete, and the cancel loop are all uncovered. A regression in any of these untested paths — e.g. the dead fallbacks at GoogleCalendarService.ts:254/314 that a per-credential selection test would have caught — ships silently because calendar errors are only logged; collective bookings' calendar sync breaks with no failing check.

[ADVISORY] Video-type booking references no longer persist credentialId: `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` writes undefined for video results where the previous code wrote result.credentialId. Any flow that locates a booking's video integration via reference.credentialId — such as the credential-deletion cleanup in deleteCredential.handler.ts that this same PR touches — no longer matches video references, so deleting a video credential leaves active bookings with orphaned meetings.

[ADVISORY] The outgoing booking webhook payload's destinationCalendar field silently changes shape from object|null to array, as evidenced by the e2e expectation flipping from null to []. External org-webhook consumers that read payload.destinationCalendar?.externalId (or otherwise assume a single object) receive an array after deploy and resolve every field access to undefined — their integrations break with no version bump, deprecation notice, or migration path.

[ADVISORY] update() was converted to process every calendar reference via filter, but the newBookingId merge path still uses `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))` to pick a single old reference to delete. When a booking with multiple calendar references (any post-PR COLLECTIVE booking) goes through the newBookingId merge path, only the first old calendar event is deleted and hosts 2..N's old events remain as orphans at the old time.

[BUG] The Meet-location fallback dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no undefined guard after destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so it throws TypeError whenever destinationCalendar is null or empty. Every booking with Google Meet selected made by a user who never configured a destinationCalendar (handleNewBooking explicitly sets evt.destinationCalendar to null in that case) crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)' during EventManager's create path, 500ing the booking instead of falling back to Cal Video as the old `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` check did.

[BUG] This drive-by rewrite inverts the IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, so slug is now written exactly in the flag state where it previously was not. With team billing disabled, new organizations are created with no slug at all (breaking the org routing/setup that previously worked); with it enabled, slug is now set immediately alongside requestedSlug, bypassing the billing-gated provisioning that requestedSlug exists for — none of which has anything to do with a destination-calendar fix.

[BUG] updateEvent's fallback branch computes `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` at the exact point where externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find can never match and the fallback always yields undefined. Rescheduling any booking whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy pre-refactor references, and the other_calendar path that passes `bookingExternalCalendarId ?? null`) now sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API and the update fails, where the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback updated the correct destination calendar.

[BUG] deleteEvent's fallback searches for a calendar whose externalId equals the already-falsy externalCalendarId, making the `event.destinationCalendar?.find(...)` fallback provably dead code that always returns undefined. Cancelling bookings whose reference carries no externalCalendarId now calls Google's events.delete with an undefined calendarId, so the event is never removed from the destination calendar and remains orphaned, where the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback deleted it.

[BUG] evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when both eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar are absent, and the collective team calendars are then appended via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`, which no-ops on null. For a COLLECTIVE event whose organizer never configured a destination calendar, every teammate's destinationCalendar collected in teamDestinationCalendars is silently discarded and the booking is written only to the organizer's default calendars — the exact multi-host case this PR claims to handle.

[BUG] createEvent now selects the target calendar solely via `destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` with a `|| "primary"` fallback, so a destination calendar whose credentialId is null never matches any credential. Users whose DestinationCalendar row has no credentialId — a state the old EventManager explicitly branched for and the old code served via externalId — get every event created on their Google primary calendar instead of the configured destination calendar.

[BUG] LarkCalendarService.createEvent resolves the target calendar from `event.destinationCalendar[0]` regardless of which destination/credential EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents invoked it for, ignoring the credentialId parameter the new Calendar interface added for exactly this purpose. For a collective multi-host booking with a Lark destination that is not first in the array, the per-destination create call sends the first host's calendar externalId with the wrong host's token, the Lark API call fails, and the teammate's calendar never receives the event — the multi-host fix only actually works on Google.

[BUG] Office365CalendarService.createEvent builds the events URL from `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` only, ignoring which destination the EventManager loop is currently processing. Collective multi-host bookings route every per-destination create call to the first host's Office365 calendar path (failing with the other hosts' tokens), so teammates' Office365 calendars never receive the collective event.

[BUG] BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters CalDAV calendars to `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (the first array element) only, so per-destination invocations from EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents can never select any other host's calendar. Collective multi-host bookings with Apple/CalDAV destinations create the event only on the first host's calendar (or on none when the filter matches nothing for the invoked credential), silently skipping the remaining hosts' calendars.

[BUG] The credential DB-fetch copied into handleCancelBooking omits the `app: { select: { slug: true } }` include and the appName remapping that the identical blocks in EventManager perform, handing getCalendar a credential with no appName. Cancelling a collective booking whose calendar reference points at a teammate's credential (never present in bookingToDelete.user.credentials) fetches a credential that cannot be resolved to an integration the way the EventManager copies arrange, so `calendar?.deleteEvent` silently no-ops and the teammate's calendar keeps the cancelled event.

[ADVISORY] The full rewrite of loadUsers (try/catch, HttpError 400/500 mapping, empty-dynamicUserList validation, and removal of `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the select) is implementation work with no traceability to the destination-calendar requirement. Dynamic-link bookings now load users without organization.slug (any consumer of user.organization.slug gets undefined), and error semantics shift hidden inside a calendar PR — an empty dynamicUserList now surfaces as a 500 'Unable to load users' and Prisma known-request errors as 400s — so the behavior change cannot be reviewed or reverted independently of the feature.

[ADVISORY] The new per-reference loop re-runs the recurring-cancellation block (all user credentials × all updatedBookings) once for every calendar reference, even though that block ignores the current reference entirely. Cancelling a recurring collective booking with N calendar references issues N× duplicate deleteEvent calls for the same events, pushing redundant failing (404) API responses into apiDeletes and logging spurious errors during cancellation.

[ADVISORY] The booking record still connects only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]`, so the multi-host destination calendar list this PR introduces has no durable representation anywhere in the data model. Every post-creation flow (reschedule, cancel, reminders, payment webhooks) rebuilds destinationCalendar as a single-element array from booking.destinationCalendar, so the collective multi-host state exists only in memory during the initial create and cannot be audited or recovered from the booking afterwards.

[ADVISORY] CalendarEvent.schedulingType is added to the public type and set on evt here, but nothing anywhere in the changeset ever reads it. The field is dead payload crossing the CalendarEvent boundary and its SchedulingType import widens the public type surface for no consumer, so the next reader must guess whether COLLECTIVE-only semantics were intended and the addition is untraceable to any requirement in this PR.

[ADVISORY] The same ~25-line 'fetch credential from DB and remap to CredentialWithAppName' block is hand-copied into EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents, and handleCancelBooking instead of being extracted into one helper. The three copies have already drifted — the handleCancelBooking one omits the app-slug include the two EventManager copies have — so any future fix to credential mapping (invalid credentials, missing apps) must be applied in three places and will predictably miss one.

[BUG] updateEvent's fallback branch searches event.destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals externalCalendarId, but that branch only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find() can never match and selectedCalendar is always undefined. Updating a booking whose calendar reference has no externalCalendarId (pre-refactor bookings, or references created through the no-credentialId destination path) sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API and the update fails, where the old code fell back to event.destinationCalendar.externalId and succeeded.

[BUG] deleteEvent computes its fallback by finding a destination calendar whose externalId equals the already-falsy externalCalendarId, which never matches, so the fallback is always undefined and the delete falls through to defaultCalendarId 'primary'. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId now targets the credential's primary calendar instead of the destination calendar where the event actually lives, so the real event is left orphaned while the delete 404s or removes the wrong event.

[BUG] The slug spread condition was inverted from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED while the requestedSlug metadata condition was left unchanged, flipping which deployments assign a slug at organization creation. With team billing enabled, organizations are created with slug set immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug approval flow the metadata still records; with team billing disabled, organizations are created with no slug at all and are unreachable at their org URL.

[BUG] LarkCalendarService.createEvent (and createAttendees at line 163) ignores the credentialId argument and always uses destinationCalendar[0].externalId as the calendarId, so every host's credential targets the first host's Lark calendar. For a collective booking with multiple Lark hosts, each secondary host's createEvent runs with their own token against the first host's calendarId and fails, so those hosts' calendars never receive the event — the multi-host fix only works on Google.

[BUG] Office365CalendarService.createEvent builds eventsUrl from destinationCalendar[0].externalId regardless of which host's credential is performing the insert. For multi-host collective bookings, each secondary host's credential requests /me/calendars/{first-hosts-calendar}/events with its own token and gets a 404, so those hosts' calendars never receive the booking.

[BUG] BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters the credential's own calendars down to destinationCalendar[0].externalId, an ID that no secondary host's credential has among its own calendars. For multi-host collective bookings on CalDAV/Exchange-style providers, secondary hosts' createEvent runs Promise.all over an empty calendar list and silently creates no event, so their calendars never receive the booking.

[BUG] Only evt.destinationCalendar[0] is connected to the Booking's single destinationCalendar relation, so the additional collective hosts' destination calendars pushed into the array are never persisted anywhere. Deferred-creation flows rebuild CalendarEvent from the persisted booking — confirm.handler.ts and the stripe/paypal payment-success webhooks wrap booking.destinationCalendar in a one-element array — so confirming or taking payment on a multi-host collective booking creates calendar events on only the first host's calendar and hosts 2..N never receive them.

[BUG] createEvent resolves the target calendar solely by matching destinationCalendar entries' credentialId against the passed credentialId and otherwise falls back to 'primary', so a destination calendar with a null credentialId — the case EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents explicitly supports through its integration-filter branch — never matches. Bookings whose destination calendar has no credentialId get their Google event created on the credential's primary calendar instead of the selected destination calendar, while CalendarManager still echoes destination.externalId into the booking reference, so later updates and deletes target a calendar the event was never created in and 404.

[BUG] The booking-reference mapping now takes externalCalendarId from result.externalId, but CalendarManager.createEvent only sets that field when EventManager passed destination.externalId as the third argument, and the no-credentialId branch calls createEvent(c, event) without it. Calendar references created through the destination-without-credentialId path persist externalCalendarId: undefined where the old code recorded evt.destinationCalendar.externalId, so later updates and deletes lose their calendar routing and fall into Google's undefined/'primary' fallbacks.

[BUG] For non-calendar (video) results the reference mapping now writes credentialId: undefined where the old code wrote result.credentialId, while the sibling mapping at line 209 keeps result.credentialId. Video-call booking references are persisted without the credential that created the meeting, so any flow resolving the conferencing credential from the booking reference gets undefined; the inconsistency with the sibling mapping shows the drop is unintentional.

[BUG] The recurring-series cancellation sweep takes only the first calendar reference of each remaining booking via references.find, although multi-host collective bookings now carry one calendar reference per host. Cancelling a recurring collective booking deletes the series event from only the first host's calendar; the other hosts' series events survive as ghost events at the old times.

[BUG] The recurring deletion sweep over all user calendar credentials x all remaining bookings now sits inside the loop over every calendar reference of the cancelled booking, so it executes once per reference. Cancelling an R-host collective recurring booking issues roughly R x credentials x remaining-bookings delete calls: the first sweep does the work and every additional sweep re-deletes the same event uids, producing duplicate 404 failures logged as errors on each cancellation.

[BUG] The DB fallback fetches the credential with prisma.credential.findUnique and no app include or appName mapping, unlike the parallel EventManager code that maps appName from app.slug before calling getCalendar. For team hosts whose credential is not in the organizer's user.credentials — exactly the collective case this PR targets — getCalendar receives a credential with no app identity, cannot resolve the calendar app, returns null, and calendar?.deleteEvent silently no-ops, leaving those hosts' events on their calendars after cancellation.

[BUG] The merge path still deletes only the first calendar reference of the old booking via references.find, while the rest of update was rewritten to process every calendar reference. When a reschedule merges bookings (the newBookingId path) for a multi-host collective booking, the old event is deleted from only the first host's calendar and the other hosts' old events are orphaned at the previous time.

[ADVISORY] createAllCalendarEvents awaits createEvent sequentially inside the per-destination loop, replacing the Promise.all fan-out the old multi-credential branch used. Collective booking creation latency grows linearly with host count — a five-host collective adds five serial Google API round-trips to the booker's request where the old path ran concurrent creates.

[ADVISORY] When a destination's credentialId resolves to neither an in-memory credential nor a DB credential with an app slug, the destination is skipped with no event created and nothing logged. A collective host whose credential was deleted or has no app row silently gets no calendar event for the booking; organizers discover the miss only when the host misses the meeting.

[ADVISORY] The COLLECTIVE gate is written as the raw string literal 'COLLECTIVE' (here and again at line 1071) although the same file previously used the SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE enum. The discriminator that turns the entire multi-host feature on is no longer compile-checked, so a future enum rename or new scheduling variant silently stops matching here and collective bookings revert to single-calendar behavior.

[ADVISORY] loadUsers dropped the organization: { select: { slug: true } } include from the dynamic-group user query. Any downstream consumer reading users[].organization on the dynamic-group booking path now gets undefined where it previously got the org slug — the include existed because something read it.

[ADVISORY] createEvent sets the Google event's organizer email from destinationCalendar[0].externalId even when the credential-matched selectedCalendar is a different host's calendar. Events inserted into secondary hosts' calendars carry the first host's calendar ID as organizer email, misattributing the organizer on every non-first host's event and confusing organizer-based edit rights in Google.

[ADVISORY] updateEvent sets organizer email from destinationCalendar[0].externalId regardless of which host's calendar the update targets via externalCalendarId. Every reschedule of a multi-host collective booking rewrites the organizer on secondary hosts' events to the first host's calendar ID.

[ADVISORY] The multi-host destination-calendar collection is gated on eventType.schedulingType === 'COLLECTIVE', excluding dynamic group bookings even though the removed comment explicitly named 'dynamic collective events' as needing per-member destinationCalendar handling. Dynamic multi-user bookings still create the calendar event only on the organizer's destination calendar, so the other invited users' calendars never see the booking — the exact gap this PR claims to close.

[BUG] The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration off the destructured first element with no null guard, so it throws a TypeError whenever evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array. A booking or confirmation with location integrations:google:meet by a user with no destination calendar (handleNewBooking builds destinationCalendar: null at line 1067; confirm.handler builds []) crashes EventManager.create with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)', returning a 500 and failing the booking, where the old optional-chained code fell back to Cal Video.

[BUG] updateEvent's fallback branch searches destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals the already-falsy externalCalendarId, a predicate that can never match, so selectedCalendar is always undefined in that branch. Rescheduling any booking whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy destination calendars without credentialId, pre-refactor references) now sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API instead of the old destinationCalendar.externalId fallback, so the event is never updated and the old time slot stays booked on the host's calendar.

[BUG] deleteEvent's fallback branch uses the same self-referential predicate find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) inside the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, which never matches and always yields undefined. Cancelling any booking whose calendar reference has no externalCalendarId but whose destinationCalendar is populated now passes calendarId: undefined to calendar.events.delete, so the event is silently left on the host's Google calendar after cancellation.

[BUG] The rewrite of the organization slug spread inverts its condition: ...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }) became ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}), an unrelated silent objective change smuggled into a destinationCalendar PR. With team billing enabled, organizations now get slug set immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug/isOrganizationVerified review flow (and writing both slug and requestedSlug); with billing disabled (self-hosted), organizations are created with no slug at all, breaking org routing. Neither behavior matches the accepted pre-PR semantics.

[BUG] The DB fallback assigns the raw prisma.credential row to calendarCredential without including the app relation or mapping appName, then passes it to getCalendar, which resolves the calendar service from appName (EventManager's parallel DB fetch in this same diff maps appName: app.slug for exactly this reason). For collective bookings — whose references now carry other hosts' credentialIds that are never in bookingToDelete.user.credentials — getCalendar cannot identify the app, returns no service, and calendar?.deleteEvent silently no-ops, leaving the event on every non-organizer host's calendar after cancellation while apiDeletes records undefined.

[BUG] The reschedule loop reuses the outer `credential` variable without resetting it per reference, so when a later reference's credential is missing from both calendarCredentials and the DB, the previous reference's credential is silently reused. Rescheduling a multi-host booking after one host deleted their calendar credential calls updateEvent with the wrong credential against the wrong reference uid/externalCalendarId (updating or 404-ing the previous host's calendar), and if the very first lookup fails, updateEvent(undefined) throws and the catch marks every reference as failed for the whole reschedule.

[BUG] createEvent selects the calendar via find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId), which never matches destinations whose credentialId is null, so selectedCalendar falls back to 'primary'. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The recurring-series deletion sweep over all user calendar credentials and all updatedBookings now runs once per calendar reference, and inside the sweep each updated booking is still handled via references.find, i.e. only its first calendar reference. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and the subsequent evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) then silently skips, dropping every teammate's calendar. A collective booking whose organizer has no destinationCalendar proceeds without any of the teammates' destination calendars and without any error, so no teammate calendar receives the event — the multi-host behavior this PR introduces no-ops for exactly that configuration.

adjudication.rationale:
In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is explicitly set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists:
```ts
destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : null,
```
Then for COLLECTIVE team events it tries to add teammates’ destination calendars via optional chaining:
```ts
if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") {
  evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);
}
```
If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, this push is skipped and all `teamDestinationCalendars` collected from `users.slice(1)` are dropped. That means the PR’s new “multi-destinationCalendar” behavior silently no-ops in the configuration where the organizer (and event type) lacks a destination calendar but teammates have one, which is exactly what the finding describes (at least the dropping-without-error part is directly verifiable from the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] loadUsers' new catch maps Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError to HttpError 400, rethrowing server-side database failures as client errors with the raw Prisma message. adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `loadUsers` was changed to wrap user-loading logic in a `try/catch` that explicitly maps `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` to `throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: error.message })`. This makes server-side/database failures (e.g., connection/pool timeouts) surface as client-side 400 Bad Request and forwards the raw Prisma error message to the client, which is both incorrect error semantics and an information leak. This behavior is directly shown in the added catch block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The credentialId-less destination branch calls createEvent(c, event) without destination.externalId (line ~377) while the reference writer now stores `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`, which is undefined on that branch — the old code stored evt.destinationCalendar.externalId. Bookings created through the credentialId-less destination branch get calendar references with externalCalendarId undefined, so their later update/delete falls into the GoogleCalendarService fallback that this same diff broke (undefined calendarId) — those Google events can never be moved or cancelled.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when iterating `event.destinationCalendar` entries without `destination.credentialId`, it calls `createEvent(c, event)` (no third arg) inside `destinationCalendarCredentials.map(...)`. But `CalendarManager.createEvent` was changed to return `externalId` from the optional third parameter, and `EventManager` now writes calendar references using `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` (replacing the old `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). Therefore, events created via the credentialId-less branch will produce `EventResult.externalId === undefined`, causing stored calendar references to have `externalCalendarId` undefined. This is a correctness regression directly shown by the diff and can break later update/delete routing that depends on `externalCalendarId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The recurring-event delete sweep (`bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith("_calendar")).map(...)` over updatedBookings) now sits inside the per-reference loop without being made reference-aware, so it executes once per calendar reference and still deletes only the first calendar reference of each remaining series booking. Cancelling a recurring COLLECTIVE booking with N calendar references runs the sweep N times (duplicate deleteEvent calls whose failures are swallowed by the surrounding catch) and never touches the non-first hosts' events for the remaining series bookings — those hosts' calendars keep orphaned events.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookingCalendarReference` was changed from a single ref (`find`) to an array (`filter`) and the deletion logic is now wrapped in `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Inside the `credentialId` branch, the recurring-series delete sweep (`bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith("_calendar")).map(...)` iterating `updatedBookings`) is executed for every reference, but it still uses `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`, i.e. it only deletes the first calendar reference per remaining booking. This both (a) repeats the sweep once per calendar reference (duplicate deleteEvent calls) and (b) fails to delete non-first hosts' calendar events for the series, leaving orphaned events. Errors during the sweep are caught and only logged, so duplicate failures can be swallowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff's only test change updates a serialized fixture value (destinationCalendar: []) and adds no verification of the new multi-destination behavior — the EventManager fan-out loop, Google's per-credential calendar selection, the DB credential fallback, multi-reference update/delete, and the cancel loop are all uncovered. A regression in any of these untested paths — e.g. the dead fallbacks at GoogleCalendarService.ts:254/314 that a per-credential selection test would have caught — ships silently because calendar errors are only logged; collective bookings' calendar sync breaks with no failing check.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes major behavioral changes around `destinationCalendar` becoming an array and adds nontrivial logic (e.g., EventManager `createAllCalendarEvents` now fans out over multiple destinations with DB credential fallback; booking update/cancel paths now process multiple calendar references; GoogleCalendarService `createEvent` now selects calendar per `credentialId`). Yet the only test change shown is in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts`, updating a serialized expected value from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []`, with no new assertions covering the new multi-destination fan-out/selection/update/delete behaviors. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test-gap concern rather than a style nit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Video-type booking references no longer persist credentialId: `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` writes undefined for video results where the previous code wrote result.credentialId. Any flow that locates a booking's video integration via reference.credentialId — such as the credential-deletion cleanup in deleteCredential.handler.ts that this same PR touches — no longer matches video references, so deleting a video credential leaves active bookings with orphaned meetings.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a concrete behavior change: in `packages/core/EventManager.ts` the reference payload now sets `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` (and similarly `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined`), whereas previously non-calendar (e.g., video) references would get `result.credentialId` (`... : result.credentialId`). So the finding’s core claim (“video-type booking references no longer persist credentialId”) is verifiable from the diff. However, the claimed downstream breakage (e.g., delete-credential cleanup relying on `reference.credentialId` for video) is not shown in this diff, so the orphaned-meetings impact can’t be confirmed here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The outgoing booking webhook payload's destinationCalendar field silently changes shape from object|null to array, as evidenced by the e2e expectation flipping from null to []. External org-webhook consumers that read payload.destinationCalendar?.externalId (or otherwise assume a single object) receive an array after deploy and resolve every field access to undefined — their integrations break with no version bump, deprecation notice, or migration path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `destinationCalendar` from a single object/null to an array across the `CalendarEvent` type (`packages/types/Calendar.d.ts`, `packages/core/builders/CalendarEvent/class.ts`) and updates event construction sites to emit `[]` or `[selectedDestinationCalendar]` (e.g. `apps/web/pages/api/cron/bookingReminder.ts`, `packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts`). This is a real, diff-grounded backwards-incompatible payload shape change for external webhook consumers, but it’s not provably an internal correctness defect (it appears to be an intentional refactor to support multiple destination calendars).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] update() was converted to process every calendar reference via filter, but the newBookingId merge path still uses `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))` to pick a single old reference to delete. When a booking with multiple calendar references (any post-PR COLLECTIVE booking) goes through the newBookingId merge path, only the first old calendar event is deleted and hosts 2..N's old events remain as orphans at the old time.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, calendar references were changed from a single `find(...)` to `filter(...)` and are now processed in a loop (`calendarReference = ...filter(...); for (const reference of calendarReference) { ... }`). However, in the `newBookingId` merge cleanup path immediately after, the code still does `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));` (single reference) to delete the old event. With multiple calendar references (now possible/expected after the refactor), only the first matching old calendar reference would be deleted, leaving the other old calendar events orphaned at the old time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateEvent's fallback branch computes `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` at the exact point where externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find can never match and the fallback always yields undefined. Rescheduling any booking whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy pre-refactor references, and the other_calendar path that passes `bookingExternalCalendarId ?? null`) now sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API and the update fails, where the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback updated the correct destination calendar.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the updated `updateEvent` computes:
```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
The `find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but then it tries to match `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `undefined`/`null`), which will not select a real destination calendar externalId. This regresses the prior behavior (`: event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) that would fall back to the event’s destination calendar when `externalCalendarId` wasn’t provided, so updates can target the wrong calendar or end up with an undefined selection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] deleteEvent's fallback searches for a calendar whose externalId equals the already-falsy externalCalendarId, making the `event.destinationCalendar?.find(...)` fallback provably dead code that always returns undefined. Cancelling bookings whose reference carries no externalCalendarId now calls Google's events.delete with an undefined calendarId, so the event is never removed from the destination calendar and remains orphaned, where the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback deleted it.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `deleteEvent` now computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the fallback branch), the `.find(...)` predicate compares `cal.externalId` to the already-falsy `externalCalendarId` (e.g., `undefined`/`null`), which cannot match the real destination calendar externalId in normal cases, so the fallback returns `undefined`. Previously it fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (single DC), so this is a concrete regression that will prevent deleting from the intended destination calendar when the reference lacks `externalCalendarId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when both eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar are absent, and the collective team calendars are then appended via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`, which no-ops on null. For a COLLECTIVE event whose organizer never configured a destination calendar, every teammate's destinationCalendar collected in teamDestinationCalendars is silently discarded and the booking is written only to the organizer's default calendars — the exact multi-host case this PR claims to handle.

adjudication.rationale:
In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists:
```ts
destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [..] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [..] : null,
```
Then for COLLECTIVE team event types, teammate calendars are appended via optional chaining:
```ts
if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") {
  evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);
}
```
If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, the `push` no-ops and all collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are dropped. Downstream, `createAllCalendarEvents` only iterates destinations when `event.destinationCalendar && event.destinationCalendar.length > 0`; otherwise it falls back to creating events via default credentials, so the teammates’ destination calendars won’t be used in this edge case. This is a real behavioral defect exposed by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] createEvent now selects the target calendar solely via `destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` with a `|| "primary"` fallback, so a destination calendar whose credentialId is null never matches any credential. Users whose DestinationCalendar row has no credentialId — a state the old EventManager explicitly branched for and the old code served via externalId — get every event created on their Google primary calendar instead of the configured destination calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the target `calendarId` is now chosen only via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and otherwise falls back to `"primary"` (see `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). But `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` explicitly supports destination calendars with *no* `credentialId` (the `else` branch when `destination.credentialId` is falsy) and still passes the same `event` containing destinationCalendar entries that may have `credentialId` unset. In that case, Google createEvent will never find a matching destination calendar and will create the event on the primary calendar instead of the configured destination calendar externalId—whereas the old code used `destinationCalendar.externalId` directly regardless of credentialId.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] LarkCalendarService.createEvent resolves the target calendar from `event.destinationCalendar[0]` regardless of which destination/credential EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents invoked it for, ignoring the credentialId parameter the new Calendar interface added for exactly this purpose. For a collective multi-host booking with a Lark destination that is not first in the array, the per-destination create call sends the first host's calendar externalId with the wrong host's token, the Lark API call fails, and the teammate's calendar never receives the event — the multi-host fix only actually works on Google.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Calendar interface to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts) and updates CalendarManager to call `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts). GoogleCalendarService uses this `credentialId` to select the matching destination calendar (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`). However, LarkCalendarService was changed to always pick the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`) and its `createEvent` method still does not accept/use `credentialId` (packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). Since EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now iterates over `event.destinationCalendar` and invokes createEvent per destination/credential, Lark will still use `destinationCalendar[0]` for every call, which can mismatch the credential token and target calendar for non-first hosts in multi-destination scenarios.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Office365CalendarService.createEvent builds the events URL from `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` only, ignoring which destination the EventManager loop is currently processing. Collective multi-host bookings route every per-destination create call to the first host's Office365 calendar path (failing with the other hosts' tokens), so teammates' Office365 calendars never receive the collective event.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, collective bookings now build `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array (e.g. `handleNewBooking` pushes teammates’ destination calendars for COLLECTIVE). `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` then loops `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`, intending to create one event per destination/credential. However `CalendarManager.createEvent` does not pass that `externalId` into provider `createEvent`; it calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. In `Office365CalendarService.createEvent`, the calendar path is built from only the first destination calendar: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and `eventsUrl = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? /me/calendars/{...}/events : /me/calendar/events`. So when the EventManager loop is processing a non-first destination, Office365 still targets the first host’s calendar id, which can mismatch the token/credential being used and prevent teammates’ Office365 calendars from receiving the event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters CalDAV calendars to `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (the first array element) only, so per-destination invocations from EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents can never select any other host's calendar. Collective multi-host bookings with Apple/CalDAV destinations create the event only on the first host's calendar (or on none when the filter matches nothing for the invoked credential), silently skipping the remaining hosts' calendars.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (BaseCalendarService.createEvent), the CalDAV calendar selection is hard-coded to the first destination calendar: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then `.filter((c) => mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : true)`. Meanwhile `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` per destination, but BaseCalendarService ignores any per-invocation destination/externalId and will always filter by the first array element. This means multi-destination collective bookings can only create on the first host’s CalDAV/Apple calendar (or none if the first externalId isn’t present for the invoked credential), skipping the rest.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The credential DB-fetch copied into handleCancelBooking omits the `app: { select: { slug: true } }` include and the appName remapping that the identical blocks in EventManager perform, handing getCalendar a credential with no appName. Cancelling a collective booking whose calendar reference points at a teammate's credential (never present in bookingToDelete.user.credentials) fetches a credential that cannot be resolved to an integration the way the EventManager copies arrange, so `calendar?.deleteEvent` silently no-ops and the teammate's calendar keeps the cancelled event.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `handleCancelBooking` now falls back to `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` and then passes that raw credential to `getCalendar(...)`. Unlike the newly-added DB-fetch blocks in `EventManager` (e.g. `createAllCalendarEvents` / `updateBooking`), it does not `include: { app: { select: { slug: true }}}` nor remap into a `CredentialWithAppName` shape with `appName: credentialFromDB.app.slug`. This inconsistency is verifiable in the diff and could plausibly affect integration resolution when the credential isn’t already in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, but the diff alone doesn’t prove that `getCalendar` requires `appName` (or that `deleteEvent` will silently no-op) in this codepath.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The full rewrite of loadUsers (try/catch, HttpError 400/500 mapping, empty-dynamicUserList validation, and removal of `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the select) is implementation work with no traceability to the destination-calendar requirement. Dynamic-link bookings now load users without organization.slug (any consumer of user.organization.slug gets undefined), and error semantics shift hidden inside a calendar PR — an empty dynamicUserList now surfaces as a 500 'Unable to load users' and Prisma known-request errors as 400s — so the behavior change cannot be reviewed or reverted independently of the feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a substantial rewrite of `loadUsers` in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts` (added try/catch, new validation for `dynamicUserList`, and new HttpError mapping) that is not directly tied to the destinationCalendar-array changes elsewhere. It also removes `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the Prisma `select`, which is a real behavioral/data-shape change (users returned from `loadUsers` no longer include `organization.slug`). Additionally, an empty/invalid `dynamicUserList` now throws a generic `Error` and is converted to a 500 `HttpError` (“Unable to load users”), whereas previously `findMany({ username: { in: dynamicUserList }})` with an empty array would likely return `[]` without an exception—this is a semantics change embedded in the same PR. These are concrete scope/traceability concerns grounded in the diff, but the diff alone doesn’t prove a definite runtime break in downstream consumers, so it’s better classified as a non-bug review issue rather than a verified defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new per-reference loop re-runs the recurring-cancellation block (all user credentials × all updatedBookings) once for every calendar reference, even though that block ignores the current reference entirely. Cancelling a recurring collective booking with N calendar references issues N× duplicate deleteEvent calls for the same events, pushing redundant failing (404) API responses into apiDeletes and logging spurious errors during cancellation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, the recurring-event deletion logic is now inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` and guarded only by `if (credentialId) { ... if (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent ... ) { ... } }`. That recurring block iterates over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith("_calendar"))` and over `updatedBookings`, deleting `bookingRef` events, and does not use the current `reference`’s `uid/externalCalendarId` at all. Therefore, when there are multiple `_calendar` references (N), the same nested deletions are executed N times, causing duplicated `deleteEvent` calls and duplicated entries pushed into `apiDeletes`, consistent with redundant 404s/log noise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The booking record still connects only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]`, so the multi-host destination calendar list this PR introduces has no durable representation anywhere in the data model. Every post-creation flow (reschedule, cancel, reminders, payment webhooks) rebuilds destinationCalendar as a single-element array from booking.destinationCalendar, so the collective multi-host state exists only in memory during the initial create and cannot be audited or recovered from the booking afterwards.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` changed to an array and `handleNewBooking` can push additional team members’ destination calendars (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`), but when persisting the booking it still connects only the first element (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`). Many later flows rebuild `destinationCalendar` as a single-element array from `booking.destinationCalendar`/`user.destinationCalendar` (e.g., cron reminder, Stripe/PayPal webhooks, confirm/editLocation/cancel). This is a real, diff-grounded scope/architecture concern: the expanded list is not persisted in the booking’s `destinationCalendar` relation, so consumers relying on that field won’t see the multi-host state post-create. However, the claim that there’s “no durable representation anywhere” is somewhat overstated because calendar targets may still be inferable from stored booking calendar references (`booking.references.filter(..."_calendar")`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] CalendarEvent.schedulingType is added to the public type and set on evt here, but nothing anywhere in the changeset ever reads it. The field is dead payload crossing the CalendarEvent boundary and its SchedulingType import widens the public type surface for no consumer, so the next reader must guess whether COLLECTIVE-only semantics were intended and the addition is untraceable to any requirement in this PR.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `schedulingType?: SchedulingType | null` to the public `CalendarEvent` type (`packages/types/Calendar.d.ts`) and sets `schedulingType: eventType.schedulingType` on `evt` in `handleNewBooking.ts`, but within this changeset there are no reads of `evt.schedulingType` (logic continues to branch on `eventType.schedulingType` and `isTeamEventType` instead). This makes `schedulingType` a dead field crossing the `CalendarEvent` boundary and widens the public type surface via the new `SchedulingType` import without a diff-visible consumer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The same ~25-line 'fetch credential from DB and remap to CredentialWithAppName' block is hand-copied into EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents, and handleCancelBooking instead of being extracted into one helper. The three copies have already drifted — the handleCancelBooking one omits the app-slug include the two EventManager copies have — so any future fix to credential mapping (invalid credentials, missing apps) must be applied in three places and will predictably miss one.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the same “fetch credential from DB then remap to CredentialWithAppName” logic duplicated in multiple places: in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` (new `prisma.credential.findUnique({ include: { app: { select: { slug: true }}} ... })` and manual object construction), in `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` (same include+remap block), and in `handleCancelBooking` (similar `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` fallback, but without the `include app.slug` used in the EventManager copies). That’s a concrete maintainability/consistency issue introduced by this change and the three copies have already drifted as the finding states; extracting a helper would prevent future fixes from being applied inconsistently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateEvent's fallback branch searches event.destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals externalCalendarId, but that branch only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find() can never match and selectedCalendar is always undefined. Updating a booking whose calendar reference has no externalCalendarId (pre-refactor bookings, or references created through the no-credentialId destination path) sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API and the update fails, where the old code fell back to event.destinationCalendar.externalId and succeeded.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback branch is now:
```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
Because that branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined), the `find` compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is null/undefined, so it will not match normal calendars and yields `undefined`. The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (single object) and would have produced a valid calendar id. The diff does not add a `|| "primary"` fallback for `updateEvent` like it does for `createEvent`, so this can result in `calendarId: undefined` being sent to `calendar.events.update`, breaking updates for references lacking `externalCalendarId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] deleteEvent computes its fallback by finding a destination calendar whose externalId equals the already-falsy externalCalendarId, which never matches, so the fallback is always undefined and the delete falls through to defaultCalendarId 'primary'. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId now targets the credential's primary calendar instead of the destination calendar where the event actually lives, so the real event is left orphaned while the delete 404s or removes the wrong event.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` changed their fallback calendar selection to:

```ts
externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined (the exact case the fallback is meant to handle), the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), which will almost never match any real calendar externalId. This makes the fallback resolve to `undefined`, and the subsequent code (e.g., `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` in `createEvent`, and similarly in delete/update flows) will fall back to the credential's primary calendar rather than the intended destination calendar from `event.destinationCalendar`. Given other parts of the diff now pass arrays of destination calendars and references may not include `externalCalendarId`, this can cause deletes/updates to target the wrong calendar and leave the real event orphaned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The slug spread condition was inverted from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED while the requestedSlug metadata condition was left unchanged, flipping which deployments assign a slug at organization creation. With team billing enabled, organizations are created with slug set immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug approval flow the metadata still records; with team billing disabled, organizations are created with no slug at all and are unreachable at their org URL.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, the condition for setting `organization.create.slug` was flipped from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This means when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false, the org is now created with no `slug` at all (verifiable from the diff). While the finding claims the `requestedSlug` condition was left unchanged, it was also rewritten but remains gated on `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`, so with team billing enabled both `slug` and `metadata.requestedSlug` are set, which is internally inconsistent with a “requested/approval” flow. The inversion and resulting missing slug for the non-team-billing path is a concrete behavioral regression introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] LarkCalendarService.createEvent (and createAttendees at line 163) ignores the credentialId argument and always uses destinationCalendar[0].externalId as the calendarId, so every host's credential targets the first host's Lark calendar. For a collective booking with multiple Lark hosts, each secondary host's createEvent runs with their own token against the first host's calendarId and fails, so those hosts' calendars never receive the event — the multi-host fix only works on Google.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Calendar.createEvent` to require `(event, credentialId)` (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts) and `CalendarManager.createEvent` now always calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts). However, `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` (and its `createAttendees`) still derive `calendarId` from the first element of `event.destinationCalendar` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`) and do not use any `credentialId` to pick the matching destination calendar. Meanwhile, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over `event.destinationCalendar` to create events per destination/credential (packages/core/EventManager.ts), but it passes the same `event` object (containing the full destinationCalendar array) into each create call. Therefore, for non-Google calendars like Lark, each host/credential will target `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, which can cause secondary hosts to try inserting into the first host's calendar with their own token, matching the reported failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Office365CalendarService.createEvent builds eventsUrl from destinationCalendar[0].externalId regardless of which host's credential is performing the insert. For multi-host collective bookings, each secondary host's credential requests /me/calendars/{first-hosts-calendar}/events with its own token and gets a 404, so those hosts' calendars never receive the booking.

adjudication.rationale: In `Office365CalendarService.createEvent`, the URL is built from the first destination calendar only: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` then `eventsUrl = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? `/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId}/events` : ...` (Office365CalendarService.ts). Meanwhile, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now supports multiple destination calendars and creates events per host/destination, selecting the host credential per `destination.credentialId` and calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`. However, `CalendarManager.createEvent` passes only `(calEvent, credential.id)` to `calendar.createEvent`, and Office365’s implementation does not use `credential.id` (nor any externalId) to choose the matching destination calendar; it always uses index 0. So for multi-host collective bookings where destinationCalendar[0] belongs to a different host than the current credential token, Office365 will attempt `/me/calendars/{firstHostExternalId}/events` with another host’s token, plausibly causing 404 and preventing those hosts’ calendars from receiving the event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters the credential's own calendars down to destinationCalendar[0].externalId, an ID that no secondary host's credential has among its own calendars. For multi-host collective bookings on CalDAV/Exchange-style providers, secondary hosts' createEvent runs Promise.all over an empty calendar list and silently creates no event, so their calendars never receive the booking.
matched_golden_ids: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying logic flaw: when an external calendar identifier is used, the code filters/searches a host’s calendars by an externalId that doesn’t exist for that host’s credential (e.g., using the destination calendar’s externalId), causing the lookup to fail and resulting in no calendar match (and thus no event created for secondary hosts).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Only evt.destinationCalendar[0] is connected to the Booking's single destinationCalendar relation, so the additional collective hosts' destination calendars pushed into the array are never persisted anywhere. Deferred-creation flows rebuild CalendarEvent from the persisted booking — confirm.handler.ts and the stripe/paypal payment-success webhooks wrap booking.destinationCalendar in a one-element array — so confirming or taking payment on a multi-host collective booking creates calendar events on only the first host's calendar and hosts 2..N never receive them.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed to an array and handleNewBooking.ts pushes additional collective hosts’ destination calendars into evt.destinationCalendar (teamDestinationCalendars). Later “deferred creation” paths rebuild CalendarEvent from the persisted Booking’s singular `booking.destinationCalendar` and wrap it into a one-element array (e.g., confirm.handler.ts, stripe/paypal webhook handlers), so those flows can only ever see one destination calendar and thus will create calendar events for host #1 only, not hosts 2..N.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] createEvent resolves the target calendar solely by matching destinationCalendar entries' credentialId against the passed credentialId and otherwise falls back to 'primary', so a destination calendar with a null credentialId — the case EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents explicitly supports through its integration-filter branch — never matches. But `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` explicitly supports destinationCalendar entries without `credentialId` (the `else` branch that filters credentials by `destination.integration`), and in that path it calls `createEvent(c, event)` without any externalId hint. As a result, when a destination calendar entry has no `credentialId`, Google event creation cannot select that destination’s `externalId` and will default to the credential’s primary calendar instead of the chosen destination calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The booking-reference mapping now takes externalCalendarId from result.externalId, but CalendarManager.createEvent only sets that field when EventManager passed destination.externalId as the third argument, and the no-credentialId branch calls createEvent(c, event) without it. adjudication.rationale: Verified in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`: when iterating `event.destinationCalendar`, the `destination.credentialId` branch calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`, but the `else` branch (no `credentialId`) calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the `externalId` argument. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] For non-calendar (video) results the reference mapping now writes credentialId: undefined where the old code wrote result.credentialId, while the sibling mapping at line 209 keeps result.credentialId.
