adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The recurring-series cancellation sweep takes only the first calendar reference of each remaining booking via references.find, although multi-host collective bookings now carry one calendar reference per host. Cancelling a recurring collective booking deletes the series event from only the first host's calendar; the other hosts' series events survive as ghost events at the old times.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, the recurring-series deletion path still pulls only a single calendar reference per remaining booking: inside the recurring sweep it does `const bookingRef = updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"));` and deletes only that `uid/externalCalendarId`. With this diff introducing multi-destination calendars / multi-host references elsewhere (many `.find` -> `.filter` changes for `_calendar` refs), remaining bookings can now have multiple `_calendar` references, so only the first host’s series event gets deleted and others can remain as ghost events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The recurring deletion sweep over all user calendar credentials x all remaining bookings now sits inside the loop over every calendar reference of the cancelled booking, so it executes once per reference. Cancelling an R-host collective recurring booking issues roughly R x credentials x remaining-bookings delete calls: the first sweep does the work and every additional sweep re-deletes the same event uids, producing duplicate 404 failures logged as errors on each cancellation.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookingCalendarReference` was changed from a single `.find(...)` result to an array via `.filter(...)`, and the code now loops `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Inside that loop, for the recurring + allRemainingBookings case, it still runs a sweep over **all** user calendar credentials and **all** `updatedBookings` (`bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).map(async (credential) => { ... for (const updBooking of updatedBookings) { ... calendar.deleteEvent(uid, ...) }})`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The DB fallback fetches the credential with prisma.credential.findUnique and no app include or appName mapping, unlike the parallel EventManager code that maps appName from app.slug before calling getCalendar. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The merge path still deletes only the first calendar reference of the old booking via references.find, while the rest of update was rewritten to process every calendar reference. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] createAllCalendarEvents awaits createEvent sequentially inside the per-destination loop, replacing the Promise.all fan-out the old multi-credential branch used. Collective booking creation latency grows linearly with host count — a five-host collective adds five serial Google API round-trips to the booker's request where the old path ran concurrent creates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When a destination's credentialId resolves to neither an in-memory credential nor a DB credential with an app slug, the destination is skipped with no event created and nothing logged. A collective host whose credential was deleted or has no app row silently gets no calendar event for the booking; organizers discover the miss only when the host misses the meeting.

If neither yields a `credential`, the code simply falls through with no `createEvent(...)` call and no logging/return indicating the skip. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The COLLECTIVE gate is written as the raw string literal 'COLLECTIVE' (here and again at line 1071) although the same file previously used the SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE enum. The discriminator that turns the entire multi-host feature on is no longer compile-checked, so a future enum rename or new scheduling variant silently stops matching here and collective bookings revert to single-calendar behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, the diff changes the team/collective gating from enum comparisons to raw string literals: `isTeamEventType` is now computed via `!!eventType.schedulingType && ["COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(eventType.schedulingType)`, and later the collective-specific logic checks `eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"` (also inside `teamMemberPromises`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] loadUsers dropped the organization: { select: { slug: true } } include from the dynamic-group user query. Any downstream consumer reading users[].organization on the dynamic-group booking path now gets undefined where it previously got the org slug — the include existed because something read it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] createEvent sets the Google event's organizer email from destinationCalendar[0].externalId even when the credential-matched selectedCalendar is a different host's calendar. Events inserted into secondary hosts' calendars carry the first host's calendar ID as organizer email, misattributing the organizer on every non-first host's event and confusing organizer-based edit rights in Google.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the calendar to insert into is selected by matching `credentialId` against `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar` (`find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`), but the organizer attendee email is set from the *first* destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...; email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? ... : calEventRaw.organizer.email`). When `destinationCalendar` contains multiple entries (as introduced by making it an array and by `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` iterating over them), events created for non-first calendars will still carry `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` as the organizer email, misattributing the organizer for those events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] updateEvent sets organizer email from destinationCalendar[0].externalId regardless of which host's calendar the update targets via externalCalendarId. Every reschedule of a multi-host collective booking rewrites the organizer on secondary hosts' events to the first host's calendar ID.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent()` now derives `mainHostDestinationCalendar` as the *first* element of `event.destinationCalendar` and uses its `externalId` to set the organizer attendee email in the payload (`email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? ...`). However, `updateEvent()` targets the calendar to update via the `externalCalendarId` argument, and `EventManager.updateCalendarEvent()` loops over multiple calendar references (one per host) calling `updateEvent(..., bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId)`. This means when updating a secondary host’s event (different `externalCalendarId`), the organizer email can still be taken from `destinationCalendar[0]`, matching the finding that reschedules can rewrite organizer info on non-primary host events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The multi-host destination-calendar collection is gated on eventType.schedulingType === 'COLLECTIVE', excluding dynamic group bookings even though the removed comment explicitly named 'dynamic collective events' as needing per-member destinationCalendar handling. Dynamic multi-user bookings still create the calendar event only on the organizer's destination calendar, so the other invited users' calendars never see the booking — the exact gap this PR claims to close.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking`, additional users’ destination calendars are collected specifically when `eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"` (and `isTeamEventType` is true) and then appended via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. Since `isTeamEventType` is derived from `eventType.schedulingType` being in `["COLLECTIVE","ROUND_ROBIN"]`, “dynamic collective” events (i.e., those with `schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`) are not excluded by this gate—they are exactly what the code targets. The diff also updates calendar creation to iterate `event.destinationCalendar` (array) and create events per destination in `createAllCalendarEvents`, so the claim that multi-host calendars “never see the booking” is not supported for COLLECTIVE. The finding’s assertion about excluded “dynamic collective events” misreads the implemented condition and behavior shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration off the destructured first element with no null guard, so it throws a TypeError whenever evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array. A booking or confirmation with location integrations:google:meet by a user with no destination calendar (handleNewBooking builds destinationCalendar: null at line 1067; confirm.handler builds []) crashes EventManager.create with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)', returning a 500 and failing the booking, where the old optional-chained code fell back to Cal Video.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the Google Meet fallback was changed to destructure the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];`) and then unconditionally read `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and this line throws a `TypeError` (cannot read `integration`). The diff also shows callers can produce `null`/empty arrays (e.g. `handleNewBooking` sets `destinationCalendar: ... : null`, and `confirm.handler.ts` sets `destinationCalendar` to `[]` when none exists), so this is a real crash path introduced by the change vs the prior optional-chained access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateEvent's fallback branch searches destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals the already-falsy externalCalendarId, a predicate that can never match, so selectedCalendar is always undefined in that branch. Rescheduling any booking whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy destination calendars without credentialId, pre-refactor references) now sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API instead of the old destinationCalendar.externalId fallback, so the event is never updated and the old time slot stays booked on the host's calendar.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback when `externalCalendarId` is falsy is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

Because this branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined/""), the predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` cannot match any real calendar externalId, so `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` instead of falling back to the event’s destination calendar externalId (previous behavior was effectively `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`). This makes updates for legacy references lacking `externalCalendarId` select no calendar (likely sending `calendarId: undefined` to `calendar.events.update`), breaking reschedule/update behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] deleteEvent's fallback branch uses the same self-referential predicate find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) inside the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, which never matches and always yields undefined. Cancelling any booking whose calendar reference has no externalCalendarId but whose destinationCalendar is populated now passes calendarId: undefined to calendar.events.delete, so the event is silently left on the host's Google calendar after cancellation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `deleteEvent` now computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. In the falsy `externalCalendarId` branch, the `.find(...)` predicate compares against that same falsy `externalCalendarId` value, so it will never match a real calendar `externalId` and returns `undefined`. The code then uses `calendarId` for `calendar.events.delete`, meaning cancellations/updates without an `externalCalendarId` can attempt deletion against an undefined calendar id rather than the intended destination calendar (or a safe fallback like `"primary"`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The rewrite of the organization slug spread inverts its condition: ...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }) became ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}), an unrelated silent objective change smuggled into a destinationCalendar PR. With team billing enabled, organizations now get slug set immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug/isOrganizationVerified review flow (and writing both slug and requestedSlug); with billing disabled (self-hosted), organizations are created with no slug at all, breaking org routing. Neither behavior matches the accepted pre-PR semantics.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, the condition controlling whether `slug` is written to the organization record is inverted: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This is a concrete semantic change in the diff: when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false, `slug` is no longer set at all (previously it was), and when it’s true, `slug` is now set immediately (previously it was not). This matches the finding’s claim of a silent behavior change and can break org creation/routing under the old semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The DB fallback assigns the raw prisma.credential row to calendarCredential without including the app relation or mapping appName, then passes it to getCalendar, which resolves the calendar service from appName (EventManager's parallel DB fetch in this same diff maps appName: app.slug for exactly this reason). For collective bookings — whose references now carry other hosts' credentialIds that are never in bookingToDelete.user.credentials — getCalendar cannot identify the app, returns no service, and calendar?.deleteEvent silently no-ops, leaving the event on every non-organizer host's calendar after cancellation while apiDeletes records undefined.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `handleCancelBooking.ts` fetching a credential via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` and then passing that raw row to `getCalendar(calendarCredential)`. However, the finding’s core claim—that `getCalendar` “resolves the calendar service from appName” and thus would fail without including the `app` relation / mapping `appName`—is not verifiable from this diff. In fact, prior (unchanged) code already called `getCalendar` with `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.find(...)`, which is also a raw Prisma `Credential` (no `appName` mapping shown), implying `getCalendar` likely works from `credential.type` or other fields. The EventManager DB fetch mapping `appName: app.slug` is relevant to `CalendarManager.createEvent`’s `CredentialWithAppName` path, but it doesn’t prove the cancellation path’s `getCalendar` requires `appName`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The reschedule loop reuses the outer `credential` variable without resetting it per reference, so when a later reference's credential is missing from both calendarCredentials and the DB, the previous reference's credential is silently reused. Rescheduling a multi-host booking after one host deleted their calendar credential calls updateEvent with the wrong credential against the wrong reference uid/externalCalendarId (updating or 404-ing the previous host's calendar), and if the very first lookup fails, updateEvent(undefined) throws and the catch marks every reference as failed for the whole reschedule.

adjudication.rationale: In the updated reschedule/update loop in `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the outer `credential` variable is reassigned on every iteration in the `reference.credentialId` branch (`credential = this.calendarCredentials.filter(...)[0];`), so a missing credential does not “silently reuse” the previous one—it becomes `undefined` for that iteration. The diff does show a potential separate issue (calling `updateEvent(credential, ...)` even if `credential` remains `undefined` after the DB lookup), but the specific claimed bug about reusing the prior credential across references is not supported by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] createEvent selects the calendar via find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId), which never matches destinations whose credentialId is null, so selectedCalendar falls back to 'primary'. Bookings from users whose DestinationCalendar rows have null credentialId (the legacy branch EventManager still explicitly supports at line 347) now create the event on the account's primary calendar instead of the configured destination calendar, and because EventManager's legacy branch calls createEvent(c, event) without externalId, the stored reference also has no externalCalendarId, so later updates/deletes cannot locate the event at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent` to choose `calendarId` via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and otherwise fall back to `"primary"`. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the legacy path explicitly handles destinations with no `credentialId` (the `else` branch when `destination.credentialId` is falsy) by calling `createEvent(c, event)` without providing any destination externalId context. For legacy `DestinationCalendar` rows where `credentialId` is `null` but `externalId` is set, the `.find(...)` will not match and Google will insert into the account's primary calendar instead of the configured destination calendar. Additionally, because `createEvent(...)` now returns `externalId` only from the optional third argument and the legacy branch does not pass it, downstream code that now uses `result.externalId` (instead of `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) will store/propagate `undefined` for `externalCalendarId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] LarkCalendarService.createEvent ignores the new credentialId parameter and always uses the first destination calendar's externalId as calendarId (createAttendees at line 164 repeats this). For a collective event with two Lark hosts, the second host's createEvent call sends the first host's calendarId with the second host's token, Lark rejects it, CalendarManager's catch swallows the error, and the second host's calendar never receives the event while the booking still succeeds.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Calendar interface to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts) and CalendarManager now calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` for all calendar integrations (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts). However, `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` was not updated to accept/use this parameter and still derives `calendarId` from the first element of `event.destinationCalendar` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`). For collective/team events the diff now builds `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array and can push multiple destination calendars (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts). [];`) and filters the credential’s calendars by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] createAllCalendarEvents iterates all destinations while GoogleCalendarService resolves the target by find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId), which returns only the first match, so two destinations sharing one credentialId both resolve to the first destination's calendar. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] loadUsers' new catch rethrows a generic HttpError 500 'Unable to load users' without logging the original error, while the new validation throws client-facing 400s containing internal variable names. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] createAllCalendarEvents fetches a credential with prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } }) with no userId/teamId ownership scope and uses it to create calendar events, where the code it replaces only ever used credentials already present in this.calendarCredentials (the organizer's own). destinationCalendar.credentialId is client-supplied (the eventType destinationCalendar update payload stores it unvalidated), so a user who points their destinationCalendar at another user's sequential credential ID makes the server create events on the victim's Google/Office365 calendar using the victim's stored OAuth tokens on every booking, and the resulting booking reference persists the victim's credentialId for later update/delete abuse.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, when a destination calendar has a `credentialId` that is not found in `this.calendarCredentials`, the code fetches it directly from the DB via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` and then uses it to call `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`. Similar unscoped credential lookups by id were also added in `updateBooking` and `handleCancelBooking`. The diff itself verifies the unscoped lookup + usage; whether `destination.credentialId` is attacker-controlled is not proven here, but the missing authorization boundary is a real security defect if it is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The booking-update path fetches a credential by reference.credentialId via prisma.credential.findUnique with no ownership check and passes it to updateEvent, so a booking reference carrying a foreign credentialId executes authenticated calendar updates as the victim. A booking whose calendar reference stores a planted foreign credentialId (references inherit credentialId from the destinationCalendar used at creation) makes reschedule/update run with the victim's OAuth credential against the victim's calendar, modifying events the attacker's booking has no right to touch.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` the booking update path now falls back to fetching a credential directly from the DB when it can’t be found in `this.calendarCredentials`: `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: reference.credentialId } })`, then constructs a `credential` object and calls `updateEvent(credential, ...)` (same pattern also added in `createAllCalendarEvents`). The diff shows no check that the fetched credential belongs to the booking’s organizer/user/team (no `userId`/`teamId` validation against the booking context). That means any booking reference containing an arbitrary `credentialId` would cause calendar updates/deletes to run using that credential’s OAuth, which is a privilege escalation if an attacker can get a foreign `credentialId` into a booking reference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] handleCancelBooking adds a prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } }) fallback with no ownership scope and feeds the result to getCalendar/deleteEvent, where the previous code only used bookingToDelete.user.credentials. Cancelling a booking whose reference carries a planted foreign credentialId calls deleteEvent authenticated as the victim, deleting the referenced event from the victim's calendar with the victim's OAuth tokens.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, the new fallback path inside the `if (credentialId)` branch will query `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` when the credential is not found in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, then passes that credential into `getCalendar()` and calls `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`. If a booking reference contains a credentialId not belonging to the booking’s user, this code would still load and use it to authenticate calendar operations, creating an IDOR-style security risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] credential is declared outside the calendarReference loop and is never reset when the DB fallback finds no row, so a reference whose credentialId matches no credential reuses the previous iteration's credential (or undefined on the first iteration) for updateEvent. Multi-reference bookings — exactly what this PR's collective support produces — whose later reference's credential has been deleted get updateEvent invoked authenticated as the wrong host against that reference's uid/externalCalendarId, or a TypeError on undefined that aborts all remaining reference updates through the outer catch.

While the diff does show a potential issue that `updateEvent(credential, ...)` is still called even if `credential` is `undefined` (no `if (credential)` guard), the finding’s core claim about stale credential reuse is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The rewritten catch handler executes log.error("createEvent failed", JSON.stringify(error), calEvent), serializing the raw provider error object and the full attendee-laden calEvent into log output. For Google failures the rejected value is the googleapis/gaxios error whose config carries the request's Authorization: Bearer header, so JSON.stringify(error) writes the host's OAuth access token to server logs, and calEvent writes every attendee's name, email and booking answers — credentials and PII accumulating in log storage on each calendar failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts`, the catch block logs `log.error("createEvent failed", JSON.stringify(error), calEvent);`, which will emit the full `calEvent` object (including `attendees` with emails/names and potentially booking responses) into server logs on provider failures. The specific claim that `JSON.stringify(error)` will include an OAuth `Authorization: Bearer` token depends on the exact error shape from googleapis/gaxios and is not verifiable from the diff alone, but the unredacted logging of `calEvent` itself is clearly present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The boolean-spread cleanup dropped the negation — ...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }) became ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}) — inverting which deployments write the organization slug at creation. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only test modification in the entire diff is a serialization-shape fix — changing the BOOKING_REJECTED expected webhook payload from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []` — which verifies none of the behavior this PR claims to add. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateEvent's fallback branch evaluates `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` inside the exact branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate compares every externalId against a falsy value, never matches, and selectedCalendar is always undefined (the old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`). Rescheduling a Google booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId — legacy pre-refactor bookings, or any booking created through the new no-credentialId destination path in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, which calls createEvent without the externalId argument so the stored reference gets `externalCalendarId: undefined` — now calls calendar.events.update with calendarId undefined; googleapis throws 'Required parameter: calendarId' and the organizer's Google event is silently never updated.

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent, the fallback branch runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but it then does `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, comparing each `cal.externalId` against a falsy `externalCalendarId` (undefined/null/"") and therefore typically never matching, yielding `selectedCalendar` undefined. The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (now effectively the first element’s externalId), so this is a regression when references don’t carry `externalCalendarId` but `event.destinationCalendar` is populated. The diff shows multiple places now pass null/undefined externalCalendarId (e.g., EventManager builds `calenderExternalId` as null when missing), making this reachable and likely to break Google update calls that require `calendarId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] deleteEvent's fallback branch has the same dead predicate — `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` where externalCalendarId is guaranteed falsy by the enclosing ternary — so calendarId resolves to undefined instead of the destination calendar's externalId. Cancelling a Google booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId now issues the delete with calendarId undefined (or the 'primary' default), so the event on the actual destination calendar is never removed and stays orphaned on the host's Google Calendar after the Cal.com booking is gone.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` compute the fallback calendar id like:

```ts

  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
(and similarly for `calendarId` in `deleteEvent`). In the `:` branch, `externalCalendarId` is necessarily falsy/undefined, so the `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` predicate is effectively `cal.externalId === undefined` and will almost always return `undefined`, even when `event.destinationCalendar` contains a valid externalId. From the diff, call sites (e.g. `handleCancelBooking`) pass `externalCalendarId` from booking references and that value can be null/absent, making this fallback path relevant. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] evt.destinationCalendar is built with a `null` sentinel (every other builder in this diff uses `[]`), so when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` no-ops and every team host's destination calendar is silently dropped. []` handling load-bearing.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null,` around lines ~1040). Later, for COLLECTIVE team events it does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op when `destinationCalendar` is null, silently discarding `teamDestinationCalendars` collected from other hosts. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The recurring-event deletion block inside the new per-reference loop is reference-independent (it iterates all user credentials and all updatedBookings and never reads `reference`) and still uses `references.find` per updated booking, so with the multi-calendar-reference bookings this PR itself creates it executes once per reference — duplicating deletes — while never touching non-first references. Inside that loop, the recurring-event deletion branch (when `bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings`) ignores `reference` and instead iterates *all* `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(..._calendar)` and *all* `updatedBookings`, and for each updated booking it still does `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` (first match only). []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`) and ignores the passed credentialId argument entirely (packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). Therefore, when `event.destinationCalendar` contains multiple hosts’ calendars (handleNewBooking pushes team members’ destination calendars for COLLECTIVE), each per-host createEvent call will still target the first calendar, causing wrong-calendar writes and mismatched stored `externalCalendarId` (EventManager now records `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`).

[];` then uses `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` to build `/me/calendars/{...}/events`. [];` and filters CalDAV calendars with `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` followed by the unguarded `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` access throws a TypeError whenever destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, crashing EventManager.create. A booking with a Google Meet location by a host with no destination calendar (the exact 'Meet w/o Google Cal' case this fallback exists for, and the shape handleNewBooking now produces as `null` and confirm/cancel handlers produce as `[]`) throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)' and the booking creation/confirmation request 500s instead of falling back to Cal Video; the old `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` handled this case safely.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the diff introduces `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately uses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` in the Meet fallback condition. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]`, destructuring yields `undefined`, so `.integration` throws a TypeError. This is directly observable from the new code and is a regression versus the prior safe optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`). The diff also shows callers now sometimes produce `destinationCalendar: null` (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts`) or `[]` (multiple handlers), making this crash reachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] deleteEvent's fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` compares each calendar's externalId against the falsy externalCalendarId it is falling back from, so it always evaluates to undefined and replaces the working `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback with dead code. Cancelling any booking whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy pre-refactor references, or new references written by the no-credentialId path which now stores undefined) sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API, the delete fails, and the cancelled meeting stays on the host's calendar as a ghost event.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` changed the fallback calendar selection from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. In that branch `externalCalendarId` is `undefined/null`, so the `.find(...)` predicate can never match a real `cal.externalId`, making the fallback always `undefined`. This is dead/incorrect code introduced by the diff and can cause updates/deletes to target no calendar id (or fall back to a default like primary elsewhere), leaving events undeleted when `externalCalendarId` is missing on the reference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateEvent's fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` compares against the falsy externalCalendarId it is falling back from, so it always returns undefined and the previous `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback is gone. Rescheduling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API, the update fails, and the event stays at the old time on the host's calendar while the Cal.com booking shows the new time — a silent divergence for exactly the legacy bookings the old fallback was serving.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback was changed to:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

This compares `cal.externalId` against `externalCalendarId` exactly in the branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it will almost always return `undefined`. The previous behavior (pre-refactor) fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (single destination calendar) and would have selected the host’s destination calendar when no `externalCalendarId` was present. With the new array type, the code does not fall back to the first destination calendar (unlike other updated places that use `[mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...`). This is a real, diff-verifiable logic error that can cause updates to target no calendar / the wrong calendar when `externalCalendarId` is missing (legacy references).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Rewriting `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` as `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` inverts the condition, so slug is now written when team billing is enabled instead of when it is disabled. On deployments with IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false (self-hosted), organizations are created with no slug at all where they previously got one, breaking org pages/links; with it enabled, orgs get slug set immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug approval flow the adjacent metadata line still implements.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, the diff changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which reverses the condition. Previously `slug` was set when team billing was disabled; now it is set when enabled. The adjacent metadata line still conditionally sets `requestedSlug` when enabled, so writing `slug` immediately under `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` can bypass the intended requested-slug flow, and under `false` it stops writing slug at all.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] createEvent now resolves the target calendar only via `destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`, so a destination calendar whose credentialId is null never matches and the event is created on 'primary' instead of the configured calendar. Bookings for users whose DestinationCalendar rows have null credentialId (the legacy rows the EventManager's filter-by-integration fallback branch exists to serve) silently land on the account's primary calendar; the user's selected destination calendar never receives the event, where the old `destinationCalendar?.externalId` code targeted it correctly.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now selects the target calendar solely via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and falls back to `"primary"` when no match (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). In `packages/core/EventManager.ts#createAllCalendarEvents`, the legacy branch explicitly handles destinations with no `credentialId` by selecting credentials by `destination.integration` and calling `createEvent(c, event)` (no externalId passed and the destination objects may have `credentialId` null/undefined). For such legacy `DestinationCalendar` rows, GoogleCalendarService will not find a matching `credentialId`, so `selectedCalendar` becomes undefined and the event is inserted into the primary calendar instead of the configured `destination.externalId` (which the old `destinationCalendar.externalId` logic would have used).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The no-credentialId fallback branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the externalId argument, so CalendarManager returns externalId: undefined and the BookingReference built from that result stores externalCalendarId: undefined where the old code stored evt.destinationCalendar.externalId. Events created through this path are recorded in references with no calendar id, so later reschedule/cancel cannot locate the calendar — combined with Google's dead fallback this strands the event permanently on whatever calendar it was created on, leaving ghost events after cancellation.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when iterating `event.destinationCalendar` entries that *lack* `credentialId`, the code falls into the `else` branch and does `destinationCalendarCredentials.map(async (c) => await createEvent(c, event))` (no `destination.externalId` passed). But `CalendarManager.createEvent` was changed to optionally return `externalId` and `EventManager` now records `externalCalendarId` from `result.externalId` (not from `evt.destinationCalendar`). Therefore this path will produce references with `externalCalendarId: undefined`. This is a regression vs the old behavior where references used `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. The diff also shows Google `createEvent` now selects calendar by matching `credentialId`, so when the destination entry has no `credentialId`, it will likely fall back to `primary`, making later update/delete unable to target the correct calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] evt.destinationCalendar is set to null (not []) when both eventType and organizer lack a destination calendar, so the subsequent `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops and drops every team member's destination calendar. Collective bookings where the organizer has no destination calendar create no calendar events on any host's calendar — the exact multi-host scenario this PR claims to fix silently produces zero calendar events instead of falling back to team members' configured calendars.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, for collective team events the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which becomes a silent no-op when `destinationCalendar` is null, so team members’ destination calendars collected in `teamDestinationCalendars` are dropped. Downstream, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` only enters the new multi-destination loop when `event.destinationCalendar && event.destinationCalendar.length > 0`; with `null`, it won’t create per-destination events, defeating the intended multi-host behavior in this edge case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] LarkCalendarService.createEvent still declares only (event) and ignores the credentialId parameter the Calendar interface now requires, always targeting `event.destinationCalendar[0]` regardless of which host's credential is being used. For a multi-host collective booking, every host's Lark credential creates the event on the first host's Lark calendar (duplicating events there) while the other hosts' Lark calendars never receive the event; if the first destination belongs to a different integration, its externalId is sent to Lark as calendarId and the call errors out.
matched_golden_ids: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that LarkCalendarService.createEvent still has the old signature (event) and ignores the newly required credentialId, which breaks the updated Calendar interface contract. This is the same core issue described in the golden comment (even though the candidate adds more runtime impact details).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Office365CalendarService.createEvent ignores the new credentialId parameter and always builds the events URL from `event.destinationCalendar[0]`, the first host's destination calendar. For multi-host collective bookings, each host's O365 credential posts to the first host's calendar (duplicates) or 404s when the first destination's externalId belongs to another integration, and the remaining hosts' O365 calendars never receive the booking event.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Calendar.createEvent` to accept a `credentialId` (types) and updates Google to select the destination calendar matching that credential (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`). However, `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` is not updated to accept/use `credentialId` and instead does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and builds the URL from that first entry’s `externalId` (`/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId}/events`). Meanwhile, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops through `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each destination/credential, but `CalendarManager.createEvent` passes only `credential.id` into the calendar service and does not adjust `event.destinationCalendar` per iteration. Therefore, for O365 credentials in multi-destination (e.g., collective) scenarios, each create will target the first destination calendar’s `externalId` rather than the one corresponding to the current credential, leading to wrong-calendar inserts or failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Only `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` is connected to the booking, so the multi-host destination calendar list computed for collective events is never persisted anywhere in the database. Every flow that rebuilds CalendarEvent from the persisted booking — payment-success webhooks, confirm, reminders — constructs a single-element destinationCalendar from Booking.destinationCalendar, so paid or requires-confirmation collective bookings create calendar events only on the organizer's calendar and never on the other hosts' calendars.

adjudication.rationale: Diff makes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` an array and, for COLLECTIVE team event types, `handleNewBooking` appends other hosts’ `user.destinationCalendar` values into `evt.destinationCalendar` (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). However, when persisting the booking, it still only connects a single destination calendar: `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` (so only the first/organizer calendar is stored on the Booking). Later flows that reconstruct a `CalendarEvent` from a persisted Booking wrap only `booking.destinationCalendar` (singular) into a one-element array (e.g. bookingReminder, Stripe/PayPal webhooks, confirm, editLocation, deleteCredential, cancel), so the additional collective-host destination calendars are not available and events would only be created/updated for the single persisted calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `credential` is declared once outside the per-reference loop and reused across iterations, so when a later reference's credentialId resolves to nothing (credential deleted, DB fetch returns null) the previous iteration's credential is silently reused for that reference's updateEvent call. Rescheduling a multi-host booking where one host's credential was deleted updates the wrong host's calendar with a uid that doesn't exist there (404), or on the first iteration calls updateEvent(undefined) which throws and the outer catch marks every host's update failed — leaving stale events on all hosts' calendars after reschedule.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.updateBookingReferences` (around the diff starting at `let calendarReference: PartialReference[] | undefined = undefined, credential;`), `credential` is declared once outside the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop and is reassigned per iteration. In the `if (reference.credentialId)` branch, if no in-memory credential is found and the DB lookup (`prisma.credential.findUnique`) returns null (or lacks `app.slug`), the code still executes `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, ...))` without verifying `credential` is set for this iteration. Because `credential` is not reset to `undefined` at the start of each loop iteration, a failed lookup can cause the previous iteration’s credential object to be reused for the current reference, matching the finding’s “silently reused” scenario. If the first iteration fails to resolve, `updateEvent(undefined, ...)` is also possible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters target calendars by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (the first destination only) and ignores the credentialId the Calendar interface now passes for per-host selection. For multi-host collective bookings, CalDAV/Apple hosts after the first get no calendar event created — the filter matches only the first host's calendar and the other hosts' calendars are silently skipped, so those hosts never see the booking on their calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (BaseCalendarService), `createEvent` now derives `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and filters `calendars` with `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`, i.e., only the first destination calendar is considered. Meanwhile, the Calendar interface was changed to `createEvent(event, credentialId)` (see `packages/types/Calendar.d.ts`) and CalendarManager now calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` (see `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts`), but BaseCalendarService’s selection logic does not use the passed `credentialId` nor does it choose the destination calendar matching that credential. With multi-destination events (e.g., collective team events where `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` in `handleNewBooking.ts`), creating events per credential can result in later hosts’ CalDAV/iCal integrations filtering to a calendar externalId that belongs to the first host, producing an empty `Promise.all` and silently skipping event creation for those hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The outbound booking webhook payload now serializes destinationCalendar as an array (the e2e expectation changes from null to []), changing the external API contract in a single deploy with no versioning or transition period. Existing webhook subscribers that parse destinationCalendar as an object or null break on every booking event the moment this ships; there is no expand/contract phase or payload version bump to let them migrate, and the break is silent for both sides until subscribers report missing fields.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes the serialized shape of `destinationCalendar` from a nullable object to an array across the codebase (`CalendarEvent` type changed to `DestinationCalendar[] | null` in `packages/types/Calendar.d.ts` and `packages/core/builders/CalendarEvent/class.ts`). The webhook e2e expectation in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts` is updated from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []`, indicating the outbound webhook payload format changed. The diff does not show any webhook payload versioning, backward-compatible dual-field support, or transition/expand-contract mechanism, so the advisory about a breaking external contract is a valid, diff-grounded concern, though not a functional defect within the PR itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] This release switches calendar handling from a single `.find()` reference to multiple `.filter()`ed `_calendar` reference rows per booking, but the previous release's cancel/update readers still process only the first reference they find. A rollback to the previous release (standard incident response) or an old pod serving during a rolling deploy leaves every non-first host's calendar event un-updated and un-deleted — ghost events at the old time on all other hosts' calendars for every collective booking created while this code was live, with no cleanup path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes bookings to potentially have multiple `_calendar` references (e.g., `createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates over `event.destinationCalendar` and can create multiple calendar events/references, and `destinationCalendar` is now an array type). This diff also updates cancel/update paths to use `.filter(...includes("_calendar"))` and loop over all references (e.g., `handleCancelBooking` and `EventManager.updateBookingReferences`), so the *current* code no longer “only processes the first reference”. However, the finding’s core concern is a backward/rollout compatibility hazard: data written by this release (multiple calendar references) would not be fully processed by older pods/rollback builds that still use `.find()` semantics. The diff shows no explicit compatibility/migration/guard for mixed-version deployments, making this a concrete operational risk grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The recurring-event deletion sweep (all user calendar credentials × all updated bookings) now runs once per calendar reference inside the new reference loop, so it executes N times for an N-host booking. Cancelling a multi-host recurring collective booking issues N× duplicate delete calls per remaining booking event; the first sweep succeeds and the rest fail with 404/410 that the try/catch swallows, flooding error logs, risking provider rate limits, and masking genuine deletion failures.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookingCalendarReference` changed from a single `.find(...)` result to an array via `.filter(...)`, and the code now iterates `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. The recurring-event deletion sweep (`bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).map(async (credential) => { ... for (const updBooking of updatedBookings) { ... calendar?.deleteEvent(...) } })`) is inside that per-reference loop. Therefore, when there are multiple calendar references (e.g., multi-host booking), the sweep is executed once per reference, causing duplicate `deleteEvent` calls for the same `updatedBookings` across the same credential set. This duplication is directly introduced by the new loop structure in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] EventManager.create reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining after destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so it throws a TypeError whenever destinationCalendar is null or empty. A booking whose event type and organizer have no destinationCalendar (handleNewBooking.ts in this diff explicitly sets destinationCalendar: null in that case) with a Google Meet location crashes EventManager.create with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)', failing the whole booking with a 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video as the previous null-safe `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` check did.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the diff changes the Google Meet fallback check to destructure `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then read `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` will throw a TypeError. This is reachable because `handleNewBooking.ts` in the diff explicitly sets `destinationCalendar: ... : null` when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar, so a Meet location booking would crash instead of falling back.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Rewriting `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` as `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` inverts the condition, so the slug is now written exactly in the cases where it previously was not. On instances with IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false (self-hosted), organizations are created with no slug at all — Organization.slug is a required unique column, so the Prisma create throws and every organization creation fails with a 500; with billing enabled, orgs get their slug immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug verification flow that the very next line still encodes.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, the diff changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which flips the condition: `slug` is now written when team billing *is enabled* instead of when it is disabled. The next line still writes `metadata.requestedSlug` only when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is true, so with billing enabled the code now sets both `slug` and `requestedSlug`, whereas previously it did not set `slug` in that branch. With billing disabled, `slug` is no longer provided at all by this handler. This is a concrete behavioral inversion introduced by the diff and can break org creation if `slug` is required.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The DB fallback assigns the raw prisma.credential record — fetched without the app relation and without the appName data getCalendar needs to resolve the calendar app (the parallel fallback added in EventManager.ts in this same diff builds a synthetic credential with appName: app.slug for exactly this reason) — so getCalendar(calendarCredential) returns null. Cancelling a collective booking whose calendar references point at team members' credentials (which are never in bookingToDelete.user.credentials, so this fallback is the norm for multi-host bookings) silently no-ops: `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` pushes undefined, the booking is cancelled in the DB and cancellation emails go out, but the non-organizer hosts' calendar events are never deleted and no error is surfaced anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, when a referenced `credentialId` isn’t found in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, the new fallback fetches it via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` and then assigns the raw Prisma credential record to `calendarCredential`, which is passed to `getCalendar(calendarCredential)`. Unlike the parallel fallback added in `EventManager.ts` (which explicitly `include`s `app.slug` and synthesizes a `CredentialWithAppName` with `appName: credentialFromDB.app.slug`), this fallback provides no `appName` (and no `app` relation). Given the diff shows other new logic needing `appName` to resolve the calendar integration, this makes `getCalendar(...)` plausibly return `null/undefined`, causing `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` to no-op and pushing `undefined` into `apiDeletes` without surfacing an error—so referenced hosts’ calendar events may not be deleted during cancellation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateEvent's fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it compares every destination's externalId against a falsy value and can never match, making selectedCalendar always undefined on that path. Rescheduling any booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId while the event still carries a destinationCalendar (bookings created through the no-credentialId destination branch, which stores no externalId, plus all legacy references) now passes calendarId: undefined to calendar.events.update — googleapis rejects with 'Missing required parameter: calendarId' — whereas the old code fell back to event.destinationCalendar.externalId and the update succeeded, leaving the Google event with the stale time.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the updated `updateEvent` fallback is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

This fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but then it searches for a destination calendar whose `externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), which will not match normal destination calendars and yields `undefined`. Previously the fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (single object), which would provide a valid calendar id when references lacked `externalCalendarId`. The new logic therefore can make `selectedCalendar` undefined in cases where `externalCalendarId` is missing but `event.destinationCalendar` is present, and the diff does not show any default-to-"primary" for `events.update` like `createEvent` does, so this is a correctness regression consistent with the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] deleteEvent's fallback has the same dead find — it searches for a destination whose externalId equals the falsy externalCalendarId — so calendarId is undefined whenever externalCalendarId is not passed. Cancelling bookings whose references lack externalCalendarId now makes calendar.events.delete reject with 'Missing required parameter: calendarId', so the Google event survives cancellation (or the cancel request itself errors via the unguarded Promise.all over apiDeletes) on a path that previously deleted via the destinationCalendar.externalId fallback.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `deleteEvent` now derives `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is not passed (null/undefined), the `.find(...)` predicate compares against that same falsy value, so it will not locate the actual destination calendar externalId and yields `undefined`. The diff shows no `|| "primary"` fallback for `deleteEvent` (unlike `createEvent`, which was updated to `selectedCalendar || "primary"`), so `calendar.events.delete` can be called with `calendarId: undefined`, which matches the reported Google API error and can prevent deletions on cancellation paths where references lack `externalCalendarId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The catch block of updateAllCalendarEvents no longer logs anything: the diff deletes console.error(message) while still building `message` via message.replace that is never emitted. Every calendar update failure caught here — Google API errors, the 'Missing required parameter' rejections above, the TypeError from updateEvent being called with an unresolved credential — now produces success:false results with zero server-side log, so reschedules that silently fail to update external calendars leave operators with no trace to debug.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` within the `updateAllCalendarEvents` catch block, the diff removes `console.error(message);` and replaces the return with a mapped `success: false` result array. The code still builds/updates `message` (including `message.replace(...)`) but does not emit it via `console`, `logger`, or `log.error` anywhere in that catch. So failures handled by this catch will now return failure results without any server-side logging from this block. This is a concrete, diff-grounded observability/regression concern, but it doesn’t by itself prove a functional correctness defect (the function still returns failure results).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateAllCalendarEvents pushes `updateEvent(credential, ...)` even when credential is still undefined after both the in-memory lookup and the DB fallback fail (deleted credential or missing app.slug). getCalendar(undefined) throws reading a property of undefined, the rejected promise makes Promise.all reject, and the catch marks every calendar reference of the booking failed — one host's deleted credential blocks calendar updates for all hosts of a collective booking, with no log left behind either.
matched_golden_ids: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core bug: `updateEvent` is invoked even when `credential` remains undefined after lookup/fallback, leading to a runtime error (e.g., `getCalendar(undefined)` reading properties of undefined) and subsequent failure propagation. This matches the golden comment’s concern about needing to handle missing credentials to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] LarkCalendarService.createEvent ignores the credentialId the Calendar interface now passes and always derives calendarId from destinationCalendar[0], while EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now invokes it once per host destination. For a multi-host collective booking with more than one Lark host, every per-destination call targets the first host's calendar: the first host's event is created, and each other host's call uses their token against a calendar ID they cannot write (or a foreign-integration ID), fails, and is reduced to a log.error in core createEvent — those hosts' calendars never receive the event while the booking reports success.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Calendar interface to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates over `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` per destination. However `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` is still defined as `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` and derives `calendarId` from `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` (i.e., always index 0), with no use of the passed credentialId (it will be ignored at runtime). With multi-destination events (e.g., COLLECTIVE where `handleNewBooking` pushes multiple users’ destinationCalendars onto `evt.destinationCalendar`), every per-destination Lark call will target the first destination calendar’s externalId regardless of which host credential/token is used, plausibly causing writes to the wrong calendar and failures for other hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Office365CalendarService.createEvent builds eventsUrl only from destinationCalendar[0].externalId, ignoring which host's destination and credential the EventManager is creating for. For collective bookings with multiple Office 365 hosts, each per-destination call posts to /me/calendars/{first host's calendar}/events under the current host's token — the first host's calendar gets the event and every other host's request 404s into core createEvent's catch, so those hosts' calendars silently end up with no event for a successfully created booking.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and updates `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` to iterate destinations and call `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` per destination. However, `CalendarManager.createEvent` forwards only `credential.id` into `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`, and `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` does not use either the passed `credentialId` (it still declares `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)`) or the per-call `externalId`. Instead it always derives `eventsUrl` from the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const eventsUrl = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? ...`). In collective/team scenarios where `evt.destinationCalendar` is populated with multiple hosts’ destination calendars (see `handleNewBooking` pushing `teamDestinationCalendars`), each Office365 credential call will still target destinationCalendar[0], which can cause posting to the wrong calendar or failing (e.g., 404/403) for other hosts. This matches the finding’s described broken behavior and is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters the credential's own calendars down to destinationCalendar[0].externalId, so per-destination invocations for any host other than the first match zero calendars. For multi-host collective bookings using CalDAV, the second-and-later hosts' createEvent calls filter their own calendar list against the first host's externalId, find no match, create nothing, and the failure is reduced to a log line — their calendars never get the event while the booking succeeds.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (BaseCalendarService.createEvent), the calendars list is filtered using only the first destination calendar: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then `.filter(c => mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : true)`. Meanwhile, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates over `event.destinationCalendar` and invokes `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each destination, but it passes the same `event` object whose `[0]` destination remains the first host’s calendar. For any subsequent host/credential whose available calendars don’t include the first host’s `externalId`, this filter will produce an empty set and nothing will be created for that host even though the overall booking flow continues. This matches the finding’s described failure mode for multi-host collective bookings on BaseCalendarService-backed integrations (e.g., CalDAV).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] createEvent selects the calendar via find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId) with a 'primary' fallback, so a destinationCalendar row with a null credentialId — exactly the case EventManager routes through its else branch — has its externalId silently ignored. Users whose destinationCalendar rows have no credentialId get their bookings created on the Google primary calendar instead of the destination calendar they configured (the old code used destinationCalendar.externalId), and the stored reference carries no externalCalendarId, so the event is also unaddressable for later update/delete.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the target calendar is now chosen only via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, with fallback `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. If a `destinationCalendar` entry has no `credentialId`, this `find` returns `undefined` and Google inserts into `primary`, ignoring any configured `externalId` that might exist on that destination row (old code used `destinationCalendar.externalId` directly). This situation is reachable via `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`: when `destination.credentialId` is falsy, it goes through the `else` branch and calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing `destination.externalId`, so `CalendarManager.createEvent` returns an `EventResult` with `externalId` unset. Later, `EventManager` uses `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`, so the stored reference can lack an `externalCalendarId`, making update/delete unable to target the non-primary calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] createAllCalendarEvents has no else branch when a destination's credential cannot be resolved (absent from this.calendarCredentials and the DB fetch returns nothing or lacks app.slug), so that destination is skipped with no error, warning, or result entry. A collective booking where one host's calendar credential was deleted or its app row is missing creates calendar events for the remaining hosts only while the booking reports complete success — the affected host's calendar silently never receives the event.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when iterating `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)`, the code tries to resolve a credential from `this.calendarCredentials`, then falls back to a Prisma fetch and only builds a `credential` if `credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug`. If both resolution paths fail, execution simply falls through without pushing any failure `EventResult` or logging (there is no `else` for the unresolved-credential case). As a result, that destination calendar is silently skipped and no calendar event is created for it, while other destinations may still succeed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The recurring-series deletion block (all user credentials x all updatedBookings) now sits inside the per-reference loop, so it executes once per calendar reference instead of once per cancellation, and it iterates only bookingToDelete.user.credentials. Cancelling a recurring collective booking with two calendar references issues every updated booking's deleteEvent twice — the second pass 404s into the swallowed inner catch — and events created with team members' credentials are never touched because only the organizer's credentials are enumerated, while the cancellation reports success.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, the recurring-series deletion logic (the `bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings` branch that builds `promises` over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith("_calendar"))` and loops `for (const updBooking of updatedBookings)`) is now inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Since `bookingCalendarReference` is now an array (`filter`) and can contain multiple calendar references, this block will execute once per reference, re-enumerating the same `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and re-deleting the same `updatedBookings` events multiple times. Errors from the duplicated deletions are caught and only logged (`try { await Promise.all(promises); } catch { logger.error(...) }`), so the cancellation can proceed without surfacing failure. Also, the enumeration is limited to `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, so events created under other participants' credentials (e.g., collective/team members) are not targeted by this deletion pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The else branch runs 'create an event on every credential of this integration' once per credentialId-less destination, so two destinations with the same integration and null credentialId each trigger a full pass over the same credential set. A collective event whose organizer and a member both have credentialId-less destinationCalendar rows of the same integration gets duplicate events created on every matching credential's calendar — each calendar receives one event per destination.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the diff changes `destinationCalendar` to an array and loops `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)`. Inside that loop, when `destination.credentialId` is falsy, it executes an else-branch that filters `this.calendarCredentials` by `c.type === destination.integration` and then does `createdEvents = createdEvents.concat(await Promise.all(destinationCalendarCredentials.map(async (c) => await createEvent(c, event))))`. Because this else-branch is *inside the per-destination loop*, two (or more) destinations with the same `integration` and no `credentialId` will each trigger a full pass over the same credential set, creating duplicate events on every matching credential/calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] loadUsers' catch maps the deliberate input-validation throws ('dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty') to HttpError 500 'Unable to load users', and maps PrismaClientKnownRequestError — a server-side database failure — to a 400 carrying the raw Prisma message. A client submitting an empty or malformed dynamic user list gets a 500 instead of a 4xx validation error, and DB-level failures are reported to the client as 400s leaking Prisma error text, misdirecting both the API consumer and anyone debugging from the status codes.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts`, the new `loadUsers` wraps logic in a `try/catch`. It deliberately throws `new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` when `dynamicUserList` is missing/empty, but in the `catch` only `HttpError` or `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` are mapped to a 400; a plain `Error` falls through to `throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })`. That turns client input validation into a 500. Additionally, PrismaClientKnownRequestError is converted into a 400 with `message: error.message`, which can leak raw Prisma error text and misclassify server-side DB failures as client errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Google Meet fallback now checks only destinationCalendar[0].integration, so a collective booking whose first host's destination is not Google but another host's is gets downgraded too. An organizer who selects Google Meet on a collective event whose first destination calendar is CalDAV/Office365 while another host has a Google destination is silently switched to integrations:daily — the booker receives a Cal Video link even though a working Google calendar is available on another host.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the Google Meet fallback was changed to treat `destinationCalendar` as an array and only inspect the first element: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar") { evt["location"] = "integrations:daily"; }`. Since this diff also adds multiple destination calendars for collective events (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts` pushes additional team members' `destinationCalendar`s into `evt.destinationCalendar`), it's now possible for `destinationCalendar[0]` to be non-Google while another entry is Google. In that case, the code will incorrectly downgrade from Google Meet to Cal Video even though a Google calendar credential exists later in the list, matching the reported behavior.
